mainTopic: טרפות of the kidney, spleen, lung and jaw, the shriveled lung (חרותה), and the stripped animal (גלודה), including which remaining hide saves it.
overview: The גמרא first identifies the 'crevice' of the kidney and reports that the experts of ארץ ישראל rule like רכיש בר פפא on a diseased kidney, but not like רב עוירא on a perforated spleen, except for a hole through the spleen's thick end. A proposed rule that the kidney is always more lenient than the lung is knocked down, and רב אשי teaches that one טרפה cannot be compared to another. Next come limits on clear fluid and a set size for a shrunken kidney. The גמרא then works through the משנה's kosher cases: a missing lower jaw, a removed womb, and a lung that shriveled by the hand of heaven, with a soaking test to tell what caused the shriveling. On the גלודה, the animal whose hide was stripped, the גמרא shows that רבי מאיר took back his lenient view. A סלע of remaining hide saves the animal, with opinions on where it must be, and one question ends in תיקו. Finally, רב and רבי יוחנן argue whether hoof-hide counts, and a ברייתא about hides 'like flesh' begins to back רבי יוחנן. That ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where is the crevice of the kidney?
steps.stepSummary: After mentioning the 'location of the crevice,' the גמרא asks where exactly that spot is.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...to the location of the crevice. And where is the location of the crevice?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a line about a diseased kidney that mentions a spot called the 'crevice,' and asks where that spot is. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה depends on the damage reaching a specific place in the kidney. So the גמרא needs to pin down exactly which spot 'the crevice' means.

keyTerms.meaning: The location of the crevice, a specific spot in the kidney.

phrases.english: ...to the location of the crevice.
And where is the location of the crevice?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of the diseased kidney from before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical location of the 'crevice' in the kidney.

steps.title: The crevice is the white area under the loins
steps.stepSummary: The crevice is the white matter located beneath the loins.
steps.simpleTranslation: To the white matter that is under the loins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question and identifies the crevice as the white area under the loins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a clear physical landmark. A שוחט or inspector now knows exactly which spot the rule is talking about.

keyTerms.meaning: The white part or white matter.

phrases.english: To the white matter that is under the loins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The crevice is the white matter beneath the loins.

steps.title: The experts of the West rule like רכיש בר פפא, not like רב עוירא
steps.stepSummary: רב נחוניא reports that all the טרפות experts of ארץ ישראל rule like רכיש בר פפא and not like רב עוירא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחוניא said: I asked all the experts on טרפות in the West, and they told me: the הלכה follows רכיש בר פפא, and the הלכה does not follow רב עוירא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחוניא reports the ruling he received from the experts in ארץ ישראל on two opinions mentioned earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רכיש בר פפא said that a diseased kidney makes the animal a טרפה, and that view is accepted. רב עוירא said that a perforated spleen makes it a טרפה, and that view is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: Experts in the laws of טרפות.
The הלכה, the final practical ruling.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical ruling that settles two earlier disputes about which organ injuries make an animal forbidden.

phrases.english: Rav Neḥunya said:
I asked all the experts on tereifot of the West,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לִי הִלְכְתָא כְּרָכִישׁ בַּר פָּפָּא,
phrases.english: and they told me: the halakha follows Rakhish bar Pappa,
phrases.notes: That's his earlier ruling, in the name of רב, that a diseased kidney makes the animal a טרפה.

phrases.english: and the halakha does not follow Rav Avira.
phrases.notes: רב עוירא had said a perforated spleen makes the animal a טרפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרִי לִי הִלְכְתָא כְּרָכִישׁ בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the earlier opinions about the kidney and the spleen.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A diseased kidney makes the animal a טרפה; a perforated spleen does not (as limited in the next step).

steps.title: The ruling against רב עוירא covers only the narrow end of the spleen
steps.stepSummary: Rejecting רב עוירא applies only to a hole in the narrow end of the spleen. A hole in the thick end makes the animal a טרפה, unless a layer as thick as a gold dinar remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even regarding רב עוירא, we said the הלכה does not follow him only for its narrow end. But in its thick end, the animal is a טרפה. And if a layer as thick as a gold dinar remains there, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits the previous ruling. Rejecting רב עוירא's view applies only when the hole is in the narrow end of the spleen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The spleen is split into two zones. A hole in the narrow end is kosher. A hole through the thick end makes the animal a טרפה. But if the hole in the thick end does not go all the way through and a gold-dinar-thick layer is left, the animal stays kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: As thick as a gold dinar coin.
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב עוירא is rejected completely. A hole through the thick end of the spleen still makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.whatToRemember: Spleen: a hole in the narrow end is kosher. A hole through the thick end makes it a טרפה, unless a gold-dinar-thick layer remains.

phrases.english: And even regarding Rav Avira, we said it only
phrases.notes: He means: we only said the הלכה does not follow רב עוירא in this case.

phrases.english: for its narrow end,
but in its thick end, it is a tereifa,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אִישְׁתְּיַיר בֵּיהּ כְּעוֹבִי דִּינַר זָהָב – כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: and if a layer as thick as a gold dinar remains in it, it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ruling against רב עוירא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A spleen perforated in its thick end makes the animal a טרפה, unless a gold-dinar-thick layer remains; a hole in the narrow end is kosher.

steps.title: The West's rule: what is unfit in the lung is kosher in the kidney
steps.stepSummary: The sages of ארץ ישראל propose a general rule: any injury that makes an animal unfit in the lung is kosher in the kidney, and an injury that is kosher in the lung is certainly kosher in the kidney.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West: whatever makes an animal unfit in the lung is kosher in the kidney. For a hole is unfit in the lung but kosher in the kidney. And all the more so, wherever it is kosher in the lung, it is kosher in the kidney.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The sages of ארץ ישראל offer a general rule comparing the lung to the kidney.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their proof case is a hole (נקב): it makes the animal unfit in the lung but not in the kidney. From this they reason that the kidney is always more lenient, so anything kosher in the lung must also be kosher in the kidney (כל שכן).

phrases.english: They say in the West:
Any injury that renders it unfit in the lung is kosher in the kidney,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהֲרֵי נֶקֶב פָּסוּל בָּרֵיאָה, וְכָשֵׁר בַּכּוּלְיָא,
phrases.english: for a perforation is unfit in the lung, but kosher in the kidney,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן הֵיכָא דְּכָשֵׁר בָּרֵיאָה – כָּשֵׁר בַּכּוּלְיָא.
phrases.english: and all the more so, where it is kosher in the lung, it is kosher in the kidney.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion comparing organs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Kidney injuries are always treated more leniently than lung injuries.

steps.title: רבי תנחומא challenges the rule with pus and clear fluid
steps.stepSummary: רבי תנחומא asks whether this is really a rule: pus is kosher in the lung but unfit in the kidney. He also points to clear fluid, which is kosher in both.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי תנחומא objected: Is this a set rule? Look at pus, which is kosher in the lung but unfit in the kidney! And look at clear fluid, which is kosher both here and there.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי תנחומא attacks the West's rule by bringing a case where the kidney is actually stricter than the lung.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule claimed that the kidney is always more lenient. Pus breaks that rule, since it is kosher in the lung but unfit in the kidney. Clear fluid is listed next to it as another case to test the rule against.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it (a sharp challenge).

phrases.english: Rabbi Tanḥuma objects to this:
And is this a set rule?

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי מוּגְלָא, דְּכָשֵׁר בָּרֵיאָה וּפָסוּל בַּכּוּלְיָא!
phrases.english: But there is pus, which is kosher in the lung and unfit in the kidney!

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי מַיִם זַכִּין, דִּכְשֵׁרִים הָכָא וְהָכָא,
phrases.english: And there is clear fluid, which is kosher here and there,
phrases.notes: 'Here and there' means in the lung and in the kidney.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The West's rule that the kidney is always more lenient than the lung.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pus is kosher in the lung yet unfit in the kidney, the opposite of what the rule predicts.

steps.title: רב אשי: you cannot compare one טרפה to another
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי concludes that טרפות cannot be compared to each other, because cutting an animal in one place kills it while cutting it in another place does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Are you comparing טרפות to one another? We do not say about טרפות that this one is like that one, for one cuts it here and it dies, and one cuts it there and it lives.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי drops the West's rule completely and gives the correct approach: each טרפה stands on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'Rather' (אלא) shows that the comparison method itself is being thrown out. Each organ reacts differently to injury, so you cannot reason from the lung to the kidney. Every case must be judged by its own tradition.

keyTerms.term: אֵין אוֹמְרִים בִּטְרֵפוֹת זוֹ דּוֹמָה לָזוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: With טרפות we do not say 'this is like that'.

steps.whatToRemember: With טרפות you cannot reason by comparison. A wound in one organ may be fatal while the same wound elsewhere is not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle across the laws of טרפות: you rely on the specific tradition for each case, not on analogies between organs.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Are you comparing tereifot to one another?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אוֹמְרִים בִּטְרֵפוֹת זוֹ דּוֹמָה לָזוֹ,
phrases.english: One does not say with regard to tereifot: this is similar to that,
for one cuts it from here and it dies,
one cuts it from there and it lives.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: טְרֵפוֹת קָא מְדַמֵּית לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רבי תנחומא's challenge and rejects the comparison method of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טרפות cannot be learned from one another by comparison; each injury and each location has its own law.

steps.title: When clear fluid is really kosher
steps.stepSummary: The clear fluid that רבי תנחומא called kosher is kosher only if it is unclouded and not foul-smelling. Cloudy or smelly fluid makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Clear fluid is kosher, but only when it is truly clear. If it is cloudy, the animal is a טרפה. And even if it is clear, it is kosher only if it does not smell bad. If it smells, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds limits to the earlier statement that clear fluid is kosher. It says exactly which kind of fluid counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רבי תנחומא said clear fluid is kosher in both the lung and the kidney. Here the גמרא gives two conditions: the fluid must be unclouded, and it must not smell. If either condition fails, the animal becomes a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Clear fluid found in an organ
An animal with a fatal defect, forbidden to eat even after proper שחיטה

phrases.english: And clear fluid is kosher —
we said this only when it is unclouded,
but if it is cloudy, it is a טרפה.
And even when it is unclouded,
we said this only when it does not smell bad,
but if it smells bad, it is a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the clear-fluid case that רבי תנחומא raised in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clear fluid is kosher only if it is both unclouded and not foul-smelling. Otherwise the animal is a טרפה.

steps.title: How small a shrunken kidney can get
steps.stepSummary: A kidney that shrank makes the animal a טרפה at a set size: the size of a bean in small animals, and the size of a medium grape in large animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a kidney shrank, in a small animal the measure is a bean. In a large animal the measure is a medium-sized grape.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another kidney rule. It sets the size at which a shrunken kidney makes the animal a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kidney sizes differ between animals, so there are two measures. For small animals like sheep the measure is a bean, and for large animals like cattle it is a medium grape.

keyTerms.meaning: Small animals, such as sheep and goats

phrases.english: A kidney that shrank:
in a small animal, down to the size of a bean;
phrases.notes: Once it shrinks to this size, the animal is a טרפה.

phrases.english: in a large animal, down to the size of a medium grape.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues with the kidney, giving a new kind of defect: shrinkage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shrunken kidney makes the animal a טרפה at the size of a bean in small animals and a medium grape in large animals.

steps.title: A missing lower jaw is kosher only if the animal can still be fed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says an animal whose lower jaw was removed is kosher. רבי זירא limits this to when it can live by having food placed in its mouth or pushed down its throat. If not, it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the case where the lower jaw was removed, רבי זירא said: this was taught only if the animal can live when food is put in its mouth or pushed down its throat. If it cannot live that way, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of kosher defects. רבי זירא adds a condition to the case of the missing lower jaw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה made it sound as if losing the lower jaw never makes the animal a טרפה. רבי זירא says it stays kosher only if it can survive by being fed by hand. If even that cannot keep it alive, it is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only when, a phrase that limits a rule
Placing food into the animal's mouth
Stuffing food down the animal's throat

phrases.english: If the lower jaw was removed,
phrases.notes: This is quoted from the משנה, which lists it as a case where the animal stays kosher.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
They taught this only when it can live
by having food placed in its mouth or stuffed down its throat,
but if it cannot live
by having food placed or stuffed, it is a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the kidney topic and returns to the משנה's list of kosher defects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal missing its lower jaw is kosher only if it can survive by being fed by hand. Otherwise it is a טרפה.

steps.title: Three names for the womb
steps.stepSummary: About the משנה's case of a removed אם, a ברייתא teaches that אם, טרפחת and שלפוחית are all names for the same organ.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the case where its אם was removed, it was taught: the אם is the טרפחת, and it is the שלפוחית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a word in the משנה. A ברייתא says that the word אם means the same organ as two other names.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says an animal whose אם was removed stays kosher. The ברייתא tells us this is the organ also called טרפחת and שלפוחית, so the kosher ruling applies to that organ.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for the same organ
Another name for the same organ

steps.whatToRemember: Not every damaged or missing organ makes an animal a טרפה. The גמרא keeps adding limits: clear fluid must be truly clear, a jawless animal must still be able to eat, and each case gets its own rule.

phrases.english: If its אם was removed,
phrases.notes: Also quoted from the משנה's list of cases where the animal stays kosher.

phrases.english: it was taught: the אם is the same as
the טרפחת, and it is the same as the שלפוחית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues through the משנה's list of kosher cases, now explaining a word instead of limiting a rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The terms אם, טרפחת and שלפוחית all refer to the same organ, the womb.

steps.title: What a shriveled lung is, and when it is kosher
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says a lung shriveled בידי שמים is kosher. A ברייתא defines חרותה as a shriveled lung. It is kosher if caused by heaven and a טרפה if caused by a person, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds 'even by any creature'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the lung shriveled by the hand of heaven, the animal is kosher. The Rabbis taught: what is a חרותה? Any animal whose lung shriveled. If heaven caused it, the animal is kosher. If a person caused it, it is a טרפה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: even if any creature caused it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of חרותה and brings a ברייתא that defines it and splits it into two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us חרותה means a shriveled lung. What decides the law is the cause: shriveling from heaven is kosher, and shriveling caused by a person is a טרפה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's added words are unclear, and that sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: By the hand of heaven, from a natural cause no person brought about
By the hands of a person, caused by a human

phrases.english: And one whose lung shriveled by the hand of heaven is kosher.
The Rabbis taught: Which is a חרותה?
Any animal whose lung shriveled.
By the hand of heaven, it is kosher,
By the hands of a person, it is a טרפה.
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:
Even by the hands of any creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next case in the משנה's list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A shriveled lung is kosher if heaven caused it and a טרפה if a person caused it. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds 'even by any creature'.

steps.title: Is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר being lenient or strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is adding to. If he is adding to the kosher case, he is being lenient. If he is adding to the טרפה case, he is being strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר talking about the first part of the ברייתא, which would make him lenient? Or is he talking about the last part, which would make him strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question: which part of the ברייתא do רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's words 'even by any creature' attach to?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his words attach to the first part, then a fright from any creature, such as a lion, counts like heaven, and the animal is kosher. If his words attach to the last part, then a fright from any creature counts like a person, and the animal is a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a teaching
The last part of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree on the words 'even by any creature'. The only argument is which half of the ברייתא those words are added to, and that flips the result from kosher to טרפה.

phrases.english: A question was asked before them:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אַרֵישָׁא קָאֵי וּלְקוּלָּא,
phrases.english: Is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר referring to the first part, and so being lenient,
phrases.notes: The first part is the kosher case, shriveling by the hand of heaven.

phrases.english: or is he referring to the last part, and so being strict?
phrases.notes: The last part is the טרפה case, shriveling caused by a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's added words in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'even by any creature' adds to the kosher case or to the טרפה case

steps.title: Another version of the ברייתא shows he is strict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a version of the ברייתא in which רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's words come right after the טרפה case. This shows he is being strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as it was taught: a lung shriveled by a person makes the animal a טרפה. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: even by any creature.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a version of the ברייתא that places רבי שמעון בן אלעזר right after the טרפה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here his words 'even by any creature' come directly after 'by a person, it is a טרפה'. So he is adding to the טרפה case: a fright from any creature, such as a lion, also makes the animal a טרפה. He is being strict.

keyTerms.meaning: Any creature, including animals and not only people

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, a lung shriveled from a fright caused by any creature, not only a person, makes the animal a טרפה. Only shriveling from heaven is kosher.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it was taught:
A lung shriveled by the hands of a person makes the animal a טרפה,
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:
Even by the hands of any creature.
phrases.notes: Because his words come right after the טרפה case, he must be adding to it, which means he is being strict.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר refers to the last part of the ברייתא and is being strict

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה finds rams with shriveled lungs
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה found rams in the desert whose lungs were shriveled. He asked in the בית מדרש how to tell what caused it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה was traveling in the desert and found some rams whose lungs had shriveled. He came and asked in the study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up a practical question: how can we tell whether a shriveled lung came from heaven or from a person?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from step 12 depends on the cause of the shriveling, but when we find such an animal we usually do not know what caused it. רבה בר בר חנה's question asks how to apply the rule to real animals.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בְּמַדְבְּרָא,
phrases.english: רבה בר בר חנה was walking in the desert,
and he found certain rams
whose lungs were shriveled.
He came and asked in the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה הֲוָה קָאָזֵיל בְּמַדְבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rule itself to how to apply it in a real case
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to find out whether a shriveled lung came from heaven, so the animal is kosher, or from a person, so it is a טרפה

steps.title: The water test in summer and in winter
steps.stepSummary: The בית מדרש says to soak the lungs for twenty-four hours: in summer in white vessels with cold water, and in winter in dark vessels with lukewarm water. If the lungs go back to healthy, the animal is kosher. If not, it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told him: In summer, bring white vessels, fill them with cold water, and leave the lungs in them for twenty-four hours. If they go back to being healthy, the shriveling came from heaven and the animal is kosher. If not, it is a טרפה. In winter, bring dark vessels, fill them with lukewarm water, and leave the lungs in them for twenty-four hours. If they go back to being healthy, the animal is kosher. If not, it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The בית מדרש answers רבה בר בר חנה with a practical test that shows what caused the shriveling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lung fills out again in the water, the shriveling was not lasting damage, so it came from heaven and the animal is kosher. If it stays shriveled, the animal is a טרפה. The vessels and the water change with the season, but the test always lasts twenty-four hours.
steps.whatToRemember: A shriveled lung is tested by soaking it for twenty-four hours, using vessels and water that suit the season. If it goes back to healthy, the animal is kosher. If it does not, the animal is a טרפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This test turns the rule about the cause of the shriveling into something a person can actually check on a real animal.

phrases.english: They said to him: In the summer,
bring white vessels,
and fill them with cold water,
and leave them there for twenty-four hours.
phrases.notes: 'Them' here means the shriveled lungs, which are placed in the water.

phrases.english: If they go back to being healthy,
it was by the hand of heaven, and the animal is kosher;
and if not, it is a טרפה.
In the winter,
bring dark vessels,
and fill them with lukewarm water,
and leave them there for twenty-four hours.
If it goes back to being healthy, the animal is kosher;
and if not, it is a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה בר בר חנה's question in step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Soak the lungs for twenty-four hours (in summer, white vessels with cold water; in winter, dark vessels with lukewarm water). If they go back to healthy the animal is kosher; if not, it is a טרפה.

steps.title: The argument over an animal whose hide was removed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that רבי מאיר says a גלודה is kosher and the חכמים say it is not. Two witnesses testified that it is not kosher, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says רבי מאיר took back his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the animal whose hide was removed, the Sages taught: רבי מאיר says it is kosher and the חכמים say it is not. אלעזר the scribe and יוחנן בן גודגדא already testified that such an animal is not kosher. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: רבי מאיר took back his view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new case from the משנה, the גלודה, and brings a ברייתא about it. The ברייתא shows an argument, a testimony, and a report that רבי מאיר changed his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree. Two witnesses then back the strict view that the animal is not kosher. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר adds that רבי מאיר later accepted that view, so in the end everyone agrees it is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hide (skin) was stripped off
Testified, gave a report of an accepted ruling

phrases.english: An animal whose hide was removed:
The Sages taught: an animal whose hide was removed –
Rabbi Meir rules it kosher, and the Sages rule it unfit,
and Elazar the scribe already testified,
together with Yochanan ben Gudgeda,
about an animal whose hide was removed, that it is unfit.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Rabbi Meir took back his view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the shriveled lung to the next case in the משנה, the גלודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גלודה is a טרפה. רבי מאיר first called it kosher but later took back his view.

steps.title: Did רבי מאיר ever argue at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that 'he took back his view' means רבי מאיר once argued. Yet another ברייתא quotes the same רבי שמעון בן אלעזר saying רבי מאיר and the חכמים did not argue about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From this we learn that, according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, רבי מאיר did argue about the גלודה. But a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: רבי מאיר and the חכמים did not argue about the גלודה being unfit. רבי אושעיא, son of רבי יהודה the spice merchant, already testified before רבי עקיבא in the name of רבי טרפון that a גלודה is unfit. And if a סלע-sized piece of hide remained, it is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 17. It shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר seems to say two opposite things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'רבי מאיר took back his view' means he once held a different view. The second ברייתא has רבי שמעון בן אלעזר saying 'they did not argue,' which sounds like רבי מאיר never disagreed. The ברייתא also adds a new rule: if a סלע-sized piece of hide is left, the animal is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: A large coin, used here as a measure of size

steps.confusionAlert: Both quotes come from the same person, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The problem is not two sages disagreeing. It is one sage who seems to say two different things.

phrases.english: This implies that, according to Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,
Rabbi Meir did argue about the animal whose hide was removed?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: But it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:
Rabbi Meir and the Sages did not argue
about the animal whose hide was removed, that it is unfit,
and Rabbi Oshaya already testified,
the son of Rabbi Yehuda the spice merchant,

phrases.aramaic: לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
phrases.english: before Rabbi Akiva, in the name of Rabbi Tarfon,
about the animal whose hide was removed, that it is unfit,
and if a piece the size of a sela remained on it, it is kosher.
phrases.notes: He means a piece of the hide, about the size of a סלע coin, that was not stripped off.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּלָל דִּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר פְּלִיג רַבִּי מֵאִיר בִּגְלוּדָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's statement that רבי מאיר took back his view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking back a view implies an earlier disagreement, but the other ברייתא has the same sage saying there was no disagreement at all.

steps.title: 'Did not argue' means he did not hold on to his view
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that 'they did not argue' means רבי מאיר did not stay with his disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: What does 'they did not argue' mean? It means רבי מאיר did not stand firm in his disagreement.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the challenge from step 18 by reading the second ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They did not argue' does not mean there was never a disagreement. It means the disagreement did not last, because רבי מאיר let go of his view. So both ברייתות say the same thing: רבי מאיר once disagreed and then took back his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Did not stand firm, did not hold on

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
What does 'they did not argue' mean?
Rabbi Meir did not stand firm in his disagreement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי ״לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They did not argue' means רבי מאיר never disagreed.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They did not argue' means רבי מאיר did not keep his disagreement. He gave it up, which matches 'he took back his view.'
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that a גלודה is a טרפה. רבי מאיר once disagreed but gave up his view.

steps.title: Where must the סלע-sized piece of hide be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rule that a סלע-sized piece of remaining hide keeps the animal kosher. It asks where on the body that piece must be.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If a piece the size of a סלע remained, it is kosher. Where must it be?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ברייתא in step 18 and asks a clarifying question. This sets up שמואל's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a size, a סלע, but did not say where on the body the remaining hide must be. The גמרא wants to know the location.

phrases.english: The Master said:
If a piece the size of a sela remained on it, it is kosher.
Where?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: אִם נִשְׁתַּיֵּיר בּוֹ כְּסֶלַע – כְּשֵׁרָה. הֵיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the last clause of the ברייתא quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The location on the body of the סלע-sized piece of remaining hide.

steps.title: שמואל: along the whole spine
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the remaining hide must run along the entire spine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: along the whole length of the spine.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question from step 20. The remaining hide must be along the whole spine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The location is the spine, and the remaining hide must cover its full length. This answer raises a new question about how wide the piece must be, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the whole length

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Along the entire spine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: עַל פְּנֵי הַשִּׁדְרָה כּוּלָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The remaining hide must run along the entire spine.

steps.title: A thin strip, or a full סלע's width?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a dilemma about שמואל's rule. Is a long thin strip enough if its total area equals a סלע? Or must the strip be a סלע wide along the whole spine?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Is it enough if the strip is long and thin, so that when you add up its area it equals a סלע? Or perhaps it must be the width of a סלע along the entire spine?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about how to understand שמואל's answer in step 21. It sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read שמואל. A thin strip whose total area adds up to a סלע would be the lenient reading. A strip that is a full סלע wide down the whole spine would be the strict reading, and that needs much more hide.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised in the בית מדרש

phrases.english: They raised a question:
Is it a long and thin strip,
which, when you add it all together, comes to the size of a sela,
or perhaps it must be the width of a sela
along the entire spine?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand שמואל's answer in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the remaining hide must be a total area of a סלע, or a strip as wide as a סלע along the entire spine.

steps.title: רבי נהוראי: a סלע wide along the whole spine
steps.stepSummary: רבי נהוראי explains in the name of שמואל that the strip must be the width of a סלע along the entire spine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי נהוראי explained in the name of שמואל: it must be the width of a סלע along the entire spine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dilemma from step 22 with a direct explanation of שמואל's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נהוראי clearly says 'the width of a סלע,' so the strict reading is correct. A thin strip that only adds up to a סלע in area is not enough.
steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, a גלודה stays kosher only if a strip of hide as wide as a סלע remains along the whole length of the spine.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּפָרֵישׁ רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Nehorai explained in the name of Shmuel:
The width of a sela
along the entire length of the whole spine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּפָרֵישׁ רַבִּי נְהוֹרַאי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the dilemma of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The strip must be a סלע wide along the entire spine. A long thin strip that only adds up to a סלע is not enough.

steps.title: A second answer: the tips of the joints
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה says the remaining hide must cover the tips of the joints.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: the hide must remain on the tips of the joints.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another answer to the question of where the remaining סלע of hide must be. רבה בר בר חנה says it must be on the ראשי פרקים, the tips of the joints.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the hide must run along the whole spine. רבה בר בר חנה names a different spot: the ends of the joints. This is a separate opinion about where the saving hide must be.

keyTerms.meaning: The tips or ends of the joints
An animal whose hide was stripped off, which makes it a טריפה

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
The tips of the joints.
phrases.notes: He means the leftover piece of hide must be on the ends of the joints, a different spot from the one שמואל named.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 20, as an alternative to שמואל's answer in steps 21–23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where on the body must the סלע of hide remain?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: On the tips of the joints.

steps.title: A third answer: the area of the navel
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס, quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי, says the hide must remain at the navel.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן אנטיגנוס said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי ינאי: the hide must remain at the place of the navel.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion is given about where the remaining hide must be. This time the answer is the area of the animal's navel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have three different spots: the spine, the tips of the joints, and the navel. Each sage names one place where the saving piece of hide must be.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Antigonus

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר:
phrases.english: said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yannai:
The place of its navel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further alternative answer to the same question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where on the body must the סלע of hide remain?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At the place of the navel.

steps.title: What if only one key spot is missing hide?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל asks about hide remaining everywhere except the spine, the navel, or the joint tips.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל asked: if the hide was removed from the spine area but all the rest is there, or from the navel area but all the rest is there, or from the tips of the joints but all the rest is there, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the three spots just mentioned, רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל asks a new question. What if only that one spot lost its hide, and the rest of the hide is still on the animal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinions said the hide must remain on a certain spot. The question is whether that spot is so important that losing only that spot makes the animal a טריפה, even though almost all the hide is still there. Or maybe the spot only matters when most of the hide is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks; raises a question the sage is unsure about
All the rest is still there

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai son of Rabbi Yishmael asked:
If the hide of the spine area was removed but all the rest remains,
phrases.notes: This matches שמואל's opinion from step 21; each of the three cases matches one of the opinions.

phrases.english: if the hide of the navel area was removed but all the rest remains,
if the hide of the joint tips was removed but all the rest remains,
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a new question on the three locations named in steps 21, 24 and 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is an animal a טריפה if only the key spot lost its hide and the rest of the hide remains?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves the question without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cannot answer רבי ינאי ברבי ישמעאל's question, so it says תיקו: it stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether losing only the key spot makes the animal a טריפה. The question is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions say where the saving hide must be: spine, joint tips, or navel. Whether losing only that spot ruins the animal is a תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of step 26 with no answer.

steps.title: רב: any hide saves except the hide of the hooves
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that any part of the hide can save a גלודה, except the hide of the hooves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: all of the hide can save a stripped animal, except the hide of the hooves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב says any remaining piece of hide can keep a stripped animal kosher, except hide from the hooves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question is which kind of hide counts, not where it must be. רב holds that the hide around the hooves does not count as real hide for this law.

keyTerms.meaning: Saves; keeps the animal from being a טריפה

phrases.english: Rav said:
All of the hide saves a stripped animal,
phrases.notes: He means a סלע-sized piece from anywhere on the hide is enough.

phrases.english: except for the hide of the hooves,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הָעוֹר כּוּלּוֹ מַצִּיל בִּגְלוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic within the laws of גלודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any hide saves a גלודה except hoof-hide.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even hoof-hide saves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says the hide of the hooves also saves.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: even the hide of the hooves also saves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with רב. He says even hide around the hooves counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, hoof-hide is real hide. So a סלע of it left on the animal keeps the animal kosher.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עוֹר בֵּית הַפְּרָסוֹת נָמֵי מַצִּיל.
phrases.english: Even the hide of the hooves also saves.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ עוֹר בֵּית הַפְּרָסוֹת נָמֵי מַצִּיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב in step 28.

steps.title: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן about hoof-hide
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן whether hoof-hide saves a גלודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי asked רבי יוחנן: does the hide of the hooves save a stripped animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: רבי אסי asks רבי יוחנן directly about hoof-hide. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אסי already has a source in mind that seems to say hoof-hide is not real hide. He first asks to hear רבי יוחנן's position clearly.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi asked Rabbi Yoḥanan:

phrases.aramaic: עוֹר בֵּית הַפְּרָסוֹת מַהוּ שֶׁיַּצִּיל בִּגְלוּדָה?
phrases.english: Does the hide of the hooves save a stripped animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי אַסִּי מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that tests רבי יוחנן's ruling from step 29.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers: it saves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that hoof-hide does save.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: it saves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן repeats his view: hoof-hide saves the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches his ruling in step 29. Now רבי אסי can bring his challenge.

phrases.english: He said to him: It saves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.

steps.title: Challenge: you taught that hoof-hide is like flesh
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי points to a משנה רבי יוחנן taught, which lists hoof-hide as hide that counts like flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Our teacher, you taught us: 'These are the ones whose hide is like their flesh... the hide of the hooves!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי challenges רבי יוחנן. He quotes a משנה רבי יוחנן himself taught, which lists hoof-hide as hide that is treated like flesh.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If hoof-hide is like flesh, it is not real hide. Then how can it count as hide that saves a גלודה? The challenge comes from רבי יוחנן's own teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: Their hides are like their flesh

phrases.english: He said to him: You taught us, our teacher:
These are the ones whose hides are like their flesh –
phrases.notes: This is the opening of a משנה later in this מסכתא, which lists hides that count like meat.

phrases.english: the hide of the hooves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that hoof-hide saves a גלודה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה he taught calls hoof-hide 'like flesh', so it should not count as hide.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: that משנה is a single sage's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that he learns that משנה as the view of one sage, not the accepted law.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do not trouble me, for I teach that משנה as the view of a single sage.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. That משנה is only one sage's opinion, and he does not rule that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה that treats hoof-hide like flesh is the view of one sage, a יחיד. The majority hold that hoof-hide is real hide. So רבי יוחנן can follow the majority and say hoof-hide saves.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not trouble or provoke me
The wording of a single sage; a lone opinion

steps.whatToRemember: רב says hoof-hide does not save a גלודה; רבי יוחנן says it does. He explains that the משנה calling hoof-hide 'like flesh' is only a single sage's view.
steps.confusionAlert: 'בלשון יחיד' does not mean 'in the grammatical singular' here. It means the משנה follows the opinion of one sage, against the majority.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do not trouble me,
for I teach it as the view of a single sage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תַּקְנִיטֵנִי, שֶׁבִּלְשׁוֹן יָחִיד אֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה אוֹתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source to a minority opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be the accepted law that hoof-hide is like flesh.
steps.terutzMaskana: That משנה is a single sage's view; the majority treat hoof-hide as real hide, so it saves.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the hide beneath the tail is treated like flesh for an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It says that bad intent about an olive-sized piece of the hide beneath the tail of an עולה has the same effect as bad intent about the meat: it makes the קרבן פסול if the intent is about place, and פיגול with כרת if the intent is about time.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: If someone slaughters an עולה planning to burn an olive-sized piece of the hide beneath the tail outside its proper place, the offering is פסול, but there is no כרת. If he planned to burn it after its proper time, it is פיגול, and one who eats it is liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing the source that supports רבי יוחנן's last answer. It quotes the first part of a ברייתא, which only mentions the hide beneath the tail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hide normally does not count as part of the קרבן's meat for the laws of bad intent. Here the ברייתא treats the soft hide beneath the tail like meat, so bad intent about it can make the whole offering פסול or פיגול. This first opinion names only that one hide. That sets up the contrast with the wider list that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, which is burned entirely on the מזבח
The fat tail of a sheep
Intent to do a service outside its proper place; this makes the קרבן פסול
Intent to do a service after its proper time; this makes the קרבן פיגול
A קרבן ruined by intent about time; eating it carries the punishment of כרת
Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of bad intent. Intent about the wrong PLACE makes the offering פסול but brings no כרת. Intent about the wrong TIME makes it פיגול, and eating it brings כרת.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: One who slaughters a burnt offering
with intent to burn an olive-bulk of the hide
that is beneath the tail
outside its designated place, the offering is unfit,
but there is no כרת for eating it;
if he intended to burn it beyond its designated time, it is פיגול,
and one is liable to כרת for eating it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא behind רבי יוחנן's answer that the משנה reflects only one sage's view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that listing hoof-hide as 'like flesh' is the view of one sage only
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא whose first opinion treats only the hide beneath the tail like flesh

steps.title: The second opinion groups hoof-hide with other hides
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with a second opinion, reported in two chains of names. That opinion lists hoof-hide, the head-hide of a young calf, the hide beneath the tail, and every hide the חכמים counted as 'like flesh' for טומאה. His ruling on this list comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אליעזר בן יהודה of Evlayim said in the name of רבי יעקב, and so also רבי שמעון בן יהודה of Kefar Ikos used to say in the name of רבי שמעון: Whether it is the hide of the hooves, or the hide of the head of a young calf, or the hide beneath the tail, or any hide that the חכמים listed regarding טומאה under the heading 'these are the ones whose hides are like their flesh'...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second, wider opinion that lumps hoof-hide together with all the 'like flesh' hides. This step sets up that opinion's ruling, which continues in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion named only the hide beneath the tail. This opinion puts hoof-hide on the same list as the tail-hide and the other hides counted as 'like flesh' for טומאה. Including hoof-hide in that group is what links this opinion to the משנה רבי יוחנן was asked about. That is why רבי יוחנן can call the משנה the view of one sage.

keyTerms.meaning: The hide of the hooves, the hide this whole discussion is about
A young, tender calf whose head-hide is still soft
'Their hides are like their flesh': a list of hides that have the status of meat

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that putting hoof-hide on the 'like flesh' list comes from a specific minority chain of תנאים. That backs up רבי יוחנן's own position that hoof-hide does save a גלודה.

phrases.english: Eliezer ben Yehuda of Evlayim
said in the name of Rabbi Ya'akov,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: and so Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda
of Kefar Ikos
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording; some versions leave it out.

phrases.english: would say in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
Whether the hide of the hooves,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד עוֹר הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל עֵגֶל הָרַךְ,
phrases.english: or the hide of the head of a young calf,
or the hide beneath the tail,
or any hide that the Sages listed regarding ritual impurity
under 'these are the ones whose hides are like their flesh,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יְהוּדָה אִישׁ אֶיבְלַיִם אָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second, wider opinion that includes hoof-hide.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: This opinion groups hoof-hide, calf head-hide, tail-hide and all the 'like flesh' hides from טומאה into one list; his ruling on them continues in the next line.
